findings.title: Item.QualityFromLink cannot parse the 11.1.5+ |cnIQ<n> item-link color; tests pin the retired |cff format
findings.locations: LibKa0s/Item.lua:85; LibKa0s/Item.lua:75; tests/test_item.lua:14-16; LootHistory/core/Compat.lua:163; LootHistory tests/test_itemsetup.lua:14
findings.evidence: Pattern link:match("|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)") only matches |c+8 hex; since patch 11.1.5 item links use |cnIQ<n> (warcraft.wiki.gg ItemLink / UI_escape_sequences), so every live link on 120100 returns nil. LootHistory's Compat.GetItemInfo falls back to it for uncached items, so those drops are recorded with nil quality. All three test cases and LootHistory's fixture use the pre-11.1.5 |cff shape, so they pass anyway.
findings.remediation: C-01 (Item minor 1->2): add a rung reading tonumber(link:match("|cnIQ(%d+)")) ahead of the hex rung (anchor on digits, don't require trailing ':'); keep the hex rung for stored legacy links. Add |cnIQ fixtures, keep |cff as legacy-rung case (red under: drop the |cnIQ rung). Update docs/api/Item version-2 docs + members-2.json, test-cases.md and README badge in same commit. Smoke S-001. Consumer follow-up M6-T14: refresh LootHistory tests/test_itemsetup.lua EPIC_LINK to |cnIQ shape.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/Item.lua:85 matches only "|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)", so a live 11.1.5+ '|cnIQ<n>:' link returns nil. tests/test_item.lua:14-16 uses only the legacy |cff shape. LootHistory/core/Compat.lua:163 falls back to NS.Item.QualityFromLink when C_Item.GetItemInfo returns nothing (the item is uncached). That is the common case at loot time, so drops are saved with nil quality. This is lasting data damage, which justifies high. The remediation (a digit-anchored cnIQ rung ahead of the hex rung, with the legacy rung kept) is sound and additive.

findings.title: PageBanner/PageHeader/divider leak an AceGUI Dropdown or raw Frame plus a texture on every full page render
findings.evidence: O.PageBanner does AceGUI:Create("Dropdown") each render, O.PageHeader CreateFrame each call, drawChromeDivider creates a new texture each call; releaseLedger only Hide()/SetParent(nil)s them, never AceGUI:Release. Unbounded growth per render in 8 consumers' banner/header pages (AuraMaster, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, MultiMeters, AbsorbTracker, PanelMaster). Kit mock AceGUI never reuses widgets so no test can see it. Side issue: SetParent(nil) on a texture Region unverified.
findings.remediation: C-02 (OptionsTabs minor 3->4, new Options version key): pool PageHeader frame per ctx (ctx.__headerPool via LibKa0s-Pool-1.0, released in releaseChrome via Pool.ReleaseAll); build divider texture once per ctx (ctx.__ruleTex), hide on release, never SetParent(nil) a Region; keep ctx.__bannerWidget and AceGUI:Release it at top of next releaseChrome. Kit revision +1: mock AceGUI Create/Release per-type survey in testkit/mock_record.lua with 2-line hook in mock_base.lua. New tests in tests/test_options_tabs.lua (second render releases first dropdown; header frame reused; divider drawn once per ctx). Smoke S-002.
findings.verify_reason: The leak is real. OptionsTabs.lua:1036 calls AceGUI:Create("Dropdown") on every PageBanner render. :1117 calls CreateFrame on every PageHeader. drawChromeDivider at :577 calls edgeTexture on every call. releaseLedger at :734-741 only does Hide() and SetParent(nil), and nothing calls AceGUI:Release. testkit/mock_base.lua ~1364 documents that the fake never reuses a widget. The severity drops to medium: the growth is one frame (plus its texture or dropdown) per full page render. Only the player triggers those renders in the options window, so this is a slow leak you can reach. It is not hot-path or combat growth.

findings.title: Slash CliSet/CliReset ignore the write seam's false,err refusal and echo the unchanged value
findings.evidence: Schema.Set returns false, invalid, why on validate rejection; CliSet discards it and prints path = <old value>. CliReset likewise ignores ApplyDefault false. BankLedger passes Schema.Set directly; MultiMeters has 14 validated rows; AuraMaster hand-prints the refusal in its own wrapper.
findings.remediation: C-03 (Slash minor 14->15): capture ok, err = d.set(row.path, v); if ok == false print INVALID(path) plus indented err and return, else echo. CliReset prints new NO_DEFAULT string when applyDefault returns exactly false. Document that set may answer false, reason (nil/true unchanged). Tests in tests/test_slash.lua or new tests/test_slash_refusal.lua if over 1500 lines. Consumer follow-up M6-T13: AuraMaster wrapper becomes return NS.SetByPath(path, v) and drops its own prints; re-check other hosts' wrappers. Smoke S-003.
findings.verify_reason: Slash.lua:688 calls `d.set(row.path, v)` and discards the return value. It then echoes read(row.path), which is the unchanged old value. Schema.lua:451 answers `false, invalid, why` when validation rejects. CliReset (~:703) likewise ignores applyDefault's return. So a user sees their /set silently fail with no reason given. The remediation is additive and keeps nil/true meaning success. tests/test_slash.lua is 1327 lines, so the split-file caveat is appropriate.

findings.title: Media.RegisterLSM registers JetBrains Mono without a langmask (refused on ruRU/CJK) but still counts it; comment wrong
findings.evidence: LSM refuses a font with no langmask on non-Western clients (LibSharedMedia-3.0.lua:247-249 returns false); call passes no mask and ignores return, so on ruRU/koKR/zhCN/zhTW the face is never registered while count reports 1. Comment claims identical triples cost nothing, but each consumer registers a different path; first registration wins.
findings.remediation: C-04 (Media minor 3->4): pass LSM.LOCALE_BIT_western + LSM.LOCALE_BIT_ruRU as langmask; count a font/statusbar only if LSM:IsValid(type, name) after registering; rewrite the comment (first registration wins; every consumer's path names identical bytes). Test with fake non-western LSM in tests/test_media.lua. Smoke S-004 (ruRU + enUS).
findings.verify_reason: Media.lua:274-275 calls LSM:Register(font, name, path) with no langmask and counts it regardless. In LibSharedMedia-3.0.lua (vendored copy, ~line 245), Register returns false for a font whose langmask is nil when the locale is non-Western. Register also returns false when the key is already registered (first wins), so the comment at Media.lua:251-253 ('costs nothing', 'identical triple') is misleading. lib.FONTS holds only JetBrains Mono, which has Cyrillic glyphs, so the western+ruRU mask is correct and CJK is rightly excluded. Counting through IsValid is fine.

findings.title: A later-loading newer AceEvent-3.0 re-embed silently overwrites the Bus tracking wrappers
findings.evidence: AceEvent-3.0 upgrade loop re-Embeds every target, overwriting the six members including Bus wrappers; later registrations go straight to CallbackHandler and are never recorded, so StandDown leaves them live (anti-pattern #85 draw gate) or StandUp never replays them. Latent: needs a third-party addon shipping a newer AceEvent minor.
findings.remediation: C-05 (Bus minor 1->2): keep rec.wrap[kind]; add restamp(rec) that re-assigns any member not equal to its wrapper and adopts the new raw member as rec.raw[kind]; keep a weak-keyed created list beside held and restamp every created target in StandDown/StandUp, returning a trailing restamped count via isDown's debug seam. Document the residual window in the docstring. Test in tests/test_bus.lua simulating re-embed (red under: drop restamp). Smoke S-005. Do not fork Ace3 or use a metatable proxy.
findings.verify_reason: The mechanism is real. Bus.lua:152-184 stamps wrappers onto the members of an AceEvent:Embed'd target. AceEvent-3.0's upgrade path re-embeds every target in AceEvent.embeds, which overwrites RegisterEvent and the other members with the raw versions. From then on StandDown/StandUp no longer track new registrations. But it only happens when a third-party addon ships a newer AceEvent-3.0 minor that loads after a Ka0s addon has created targets. That minor has been stable for years, and the finding itself calls it latent. There is no current path to it, so severity drops to low. The remediation is sound, including the documented window before restamp.

findings.title: Launcher click has no disabled-state seam; three hosts hand-write the rung (a)/(b) refusal differently
findings.evidence: launcher-§2 requires a disabled left-click on rung (a)/(b) to be refused with the dispatcher's line; the one OnClick owner (anti-patterns #81) has no isEnabled field, so BankLedger, AuraMaster and AbsorbTracker each gate inside onClick in three spellings; a host that forgets writes SavedVariables while disabled (#85).
findings.remediation: C-06 (Launcher minor 1->2): add optional descriptor fields isEnabled (function) and disabledLine (function returning the Slash line); in click, when left button, onClick present and not isEnabled(), emit disabledLine() and return. Rung (c) still expressed by omitting onClick. Tests for rung (a) refused, rung (c) unchanged, right-click unchanged. Consumer follow-up M6-T12: each rung (a)/(b) host passes the two fields and deletes its hand-written gate, one commit per host. Serialize after M5-T1 (shared tests/test_launcher.lua). Smoke S-006.
findings.verify_reason: Launcher.lua:178-185 click() has no enabled gate, and the descriptor docs at :98-127 have no isEnabled field. launcher.md:32 does require a disabled rung (a)/(b) left-click to be refused. All three current rung (a)/(b) hosts do implement the refusal: BankLedger LauncherSetup:156, AuraMaster :119-120 and AbsorbTracker :160-161. So nothing is broken today. This is duplication, a design gap, with only a hypothetical future host at risk. Severity drops to low. The remediation (optional isEnabled/disabledLine, rung (c) unchanged) is sound and additive.

findings.title: 23 assertError calls only assert that something raised; four pass the expected text as the failure message
findings.locations: tests/test_launcher.lua:123-128; tests/test_kit_inventory.lua:173,182,190,202,230; tests/test_mock_ace.lua (9 calls); tests/test_loader.lua:116-117; tests/test_options_compose.lua:674-675; tests/test_schema.lua:548; testkit/framework.lua:266-273
findings.evidence: Kit.assertError(fn, msg) uses msg only as failure text and returns the raised error, which callers discard; launcher case's red-under comment claims field check that doesn't happen; kit-inventory cases can pass on unrelated raises. grep gives 23 statement-position calls. testing-§12: MUST NOT treat 'it raised' as sufficient.
findings.remediation: C-09 (kit revision +1): add Kit.assertErrorMatches(fn, needle, msg) in a new testkit/asserts.lua loaded by framework.lua (framework.lua is over the cap, don't grow it); sync tests/_kit; rewrite all 23 call sites to assert on a substring of the raised error (launcher expected strings become needles). Pass count unchanged. Fold with C-02 kit half into one kit revision.
findings.verify_reason: A grep for statement-position assertError calls gives exactly 23. They are in test_kit_inventory 173/182/190/202/230, test_launcher 123-128 (x4, where the expected text is passed only as the failure message), test_loader 116-117, test_mock_ace 119/120/137/402/403/488/617/618/629 (9), test_options_compose 674-675 and test_schema 548. framework.lua:266-273 uses msg only as failure text. This breaks testing.md:480 ('MUST NOT treat "it raised" as sufficient'). The flaw is in the tests only, with no runtime impact, so severity drops to low. The remediation is fine. The existing local helper pattern (test_lifecycle.lua:34-37 / test_bus.lua:152, which asserts on the returned err) is a zero-kit-change alternative if a kit revision is not wanted.

findings.title: Core printer.Format raises on a secret value in a numeric specifier (bug DebugLog already fixed)
findings.evidence: Args are stringified first; a secret becomes "<secret>" and %d/%.1f raises 'number expected, got string' in combat. DebugLog added a pcall + verbatim fallback for the identical failure. Latent: 0 current consumer call sites pass a numeric specifier through printer.Format.
findings.remediation: C-07 (Core minor 7->8): pcall(string.format, SafeToString(fmt), unpack(parts)); on failure join fmt and parts with spaces; emit. No floor raise. Test in tests/test_core.lua (secret into %d lands as format + <secret>; red under: remove pcall). Smoke S-007.
findings.verify_reason: The mechanism is real. In Core.lua:455-460 printer.Format stringifies every argument through SafeToString, then calls fmt:format(unpack(parts)) with no pcall. A secret becomes '<secret>', and %d on that raises. DebugLog.lua:640-658 already guards the identical failure. Ordinary numbers still format, because Lua 5.1 coerces numeric strings. The finding itself counts 0 current call sites passing a numeric specifier through printer.Format, so it is latent. Severity drops to low. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: Launcher missing-library notices repeat on every Register and are double-tagged [LibKa0s]
findings.evidence: Register is callable from OnInitialize and login, so NO_BROKER/NO_ICON/NO_MINIMAP print twice; strings start "[LibKa0s] %s:" and go through the host's tagged printer. Only reachable where broker libs are missing.
findings.remediation: Part of C-06: guard each notice with once[key] per instance; drop the "[LibKa0s] " tag from the values (keys unchanged, L overrides still work). Test one NO_ICON across two Register calls.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/Launcher.lua:198 short-circuits only when object and iconLib are both set, so every failing Register reaches emit at :203, :228 or :235 again and prints again. STRINGS at :70-75 hard-code the "[LibKa0s] %s:" prefix, and makeEmit (:79-84) hands them to d.print, the host's printer, which usually adds its own tag. The notices only fire when the broker or icon libraries are missing, so low is the right severity. One caveat for the remediation: in the DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME fallback the untagged line still carries the addon name through %s, so dropping the tag is acceptable.

findings.title: DebugLog buffer trims with O(n) table.remove(1) on every line at the cap
findings.evidence: At the 1500-line MAX_BUFFER every Add shifts 1500 slots; only under debug logging.
findings.remediation: C-11 (DebugLog minor 12->13): ring buffer with head index; BufferSize/LastLine/FindLine/CopyText walk in order. D.buffer is public: grep consumers for .buffer; keep an ordered lazily-rebuilt view or fall back to batched trim (compact every 64). Characterization cases first (testing-§13), plus '1501st line drops the first'. Smoke S-008.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/DebugLog.lua:623 runs table.remove(D.buffer, 1) once the buffer holds more than MAX_BUFFER (1500, :57) lines, so every Add at the cap costs O(n). It only happens with debug logging on, and a memmove of 1500 slots is cheap, so low (arguably info). D.buffer is a public contract: tests/test_debuglog.lua:87-142 index it directly, and :117-119 already covers eviction of the oldest lines. A ring buffer would break those tests, so the batched trim (or a kept ordered view) is the safer option the remediation already names.

findings.title: Perf gate comment says 'no metatable' but instance has one; nil-initialized fields hit __index/__newindex every sampler frame
findings.evidence: P.armed/P.recording/P.label are assigned nil so never raw keys; every onUpdate read calls the __index closure. P.on gate is raw so performance-§2 holds; cost small, only during perf runs.
findings.remediation: C-12 (Perf minor 12->13): initialize armed/recording/label as false (plain assignment works before setmetatable). Change every later nil write to false (Perf.lua:911, :921, :959, :1011, :1033, :1044) so the keys stay raw, and audit any '== nil' reads of these fields first. Rewrite the :400-401 comment: P.on is a raw field and the metatable exists only for 'suspended'. Keep the tests/test_perf_isolation.lua 0 KB pin green, and add a case asserting rawget(P,'recording') ~= nil after a window closes.
findings.verify_reason: The finding is real. Perf.lua:400-405 assigns P.armed and P.recording nil, so neither is a raw key, and :940-941 reads P.recording and P.armed on every sampler frame through the __index closure (:424-428). The P.on gate stays raw, so performance-§2 holds. The comment at :400-401 ('no metatable') is stale. The remediation is incomplete, though: rawset(P,k,false) before setmetatable only helps until the next nil write, because assigning nil to a raw key removes it and the reads fall back to __index. openWindow :911 (P.armed=nil), closeWindow :921 (P.recording=nil), :959, :1011, :1033 and :1044 (P.label=nil) all write nil. Every one of them has to write false. Readers tolerate false: :307-308 compares strings, P.LABELS[false] answers nil, and 'if not w' is fine.

findings.title: ReorderList hijacks the host row frame's OnUpdate and caches its drop line on the AceGUI-pooled container
findings.evidence: Drag poll SetScript("OnUpdate") on row.frame then clears it, overwriting any host OnUpdate; container.__ka0sDropLine rides back into AceGUI's pool keeping the first caller's lineColor, contradicting the file's own pooled-frame rule. No shipped row frame carries an OnUpdate today.
findings.remediation: Same remediation as stated (poll on the library-owned ghost frame, drop line from a library pool reclaimed in Cancel, re-coloured per list, tests in a new tests/test_widgets_reorder.lua). Change rule_ref to the Widgets.lua:783-795 pooled-frame invariant (internal) instead of events-frames-taint-§6.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. Widgets.lua:999 runs row.frame:SetScript('OnUpdate', ...) on the host's frame, and :915 and :1080 clear it with nil, which would wipe any OnUpdate the host had set. :739/:753 cache the drop line as container.__ka0sDropLine on an AceGUI-pooled container, and the colour is fixed at first creation (:748). That contradicts the file's own handle-pool rule at :783-795. No shipped row frame carries an OnUpdate today, so low is right. The rule_ref is a poor fit: events-frames-taint-§6 covers Lua over XML and object pooling for high-churn UI, not keeping library state off host-pooled frames. The violation is of the module's own documented pooled-frame invariant.

findings.title: Item quality-color map cached even when built empty; LoadItem waits a fixed 0.4s timer
findings.evidence: If first call precedes ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS population the empty map persists for the session; LoadItem fires after C_Timer.After(0.4) regardless of data arrival. Unlikely in client; less relevant once |cnIQ rung lands.
findings.remediation: Part of C-01: build into a local and assign qualityByHex only if at least one entry landed; add empty-map retry case. Leave LoadItem unchanged (byte-identical in both hosts) and record that decision.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/Item.lua:63-71: buildQualityByHex assigns qualityByHex = {} before it checks ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS, and :87 only rebuilds when the map is nil, so an empty map built early is kept for the whole session. The comment at :57-60 names exactly this failure mode, but the code only half-avoids it. LoadItem at :124 fires cb after a fixed C_Timer.After(0.4) whether or not the data arrived. It is unlikely in the client, so low. The remediation (commit only a non-empty map, leave LoadItem alone and record why) is sound.

findings.title: Schema ApplyDefault and a row's own get drop instanceId
findings.evidence: Set/Get accept instanceId via resolveRoot, but ApplyDefault calls S.Set with no id and a closure row's get() receives no id. No current consumer affected (AuraMaster keeps its own runtime).
findings.remediation: C-08 (Schema minor 1->2, optional): S.ApplyDefault(row, instanceId) forwards to S.Set; S.Get calls row get(instanceId). Additive. Review recommends deferring until an instanced host adopts the runtime and recording the deferral in CHANGELOG.md and the Schema API doc; user asked for ALL findings so plan should either implement or explicitly record deferral.
findings.verify_reason: Schema.lua:358 calls row.get() with no instanceId even though S.Get takes one. ApplyDefault(row) at :497-502 calls S.Set(row.path, ...) with no instanceId either. No current consumer is affected, so low. The additive change fits library-stack-§7 minor rules, and implementing it or explicitly recording the deferral both satisfy the ALL-findings request.

findings.title: A Perf bracket left open by an error misattributes later brackets' observed parent for the rest of the run
findings.evidence: openDepth only reset in P.Reset (from Start); a host raise between Open and Close leaves the slot open so later Close records the leaked key as observedWithin; window open/close doesn't reset.
findings.remediation: Part of C-12: reset openDepth = 0 in openWindow and closeWindow. Test in tests/test_perf_core.lua: leaked Open in window A does not parent a bracket in window B.
findings.verify_reason: Perf.lua:550 increments openDepth on Open, and Close (:569-584) only lowers it for a matched key. If a host error lands between Open and Close, the slot stays open below later brackets. The only reset is P.Reset at :592, not openWindow (:909) or closeWindow (:919), so a later nested Close reports the leaked key as its parent (:581), even in a different window. This only affects diagnostics during perf runs, so low. Resetting openDepth=0 in both window transitions is correct and allocation-free.

findings.title: Lifecycle edge is re-entrant and the file doesn't document it
findings.evidence: A standDown callback that takes/releases a hold fires a nested edge (standUp inside unwinding standDown); latch stays consistent but host teardown can interleave. No shipped callback touches the latch.
findings.remediation: C-13 (Lifecycle minor 1->2): document in New's docstring that a callback MUST NOT take or release a hold (or queue nested edges), and add a tests/test_lifecycle.lua case pinning the chosen nested-edge behavior.
findings.verify_reason: LibKa0s/Lifecycle.lua:123-129 edge() sets `down` then calls d.standDown()/d.standUp() synchronously; a Release inside standDown would re-enter edge() and fire standUp nested. New's docstring (:75-89) says nothing about re-entrancy, and grep for reentr/nested finds nothing in Lifecycle.lua, tests/test_lifecycle.lua or docs/api/Lifecycle. No shipped callback does this, so low is right. A comment change still changes the file's bytes, so the Lifecycle minor bump and a docs/api/Lifecycle update are right. This is LibKa0s's own payload, so the non-upstream routing is correct.

findings.title: Six tags cut with no release bundle naming them (release gate never evaluated)
findings.locations: docs/releasing.md:157; docs/automated-tests/*/manifest.json; tags v1.28.0, v1.29.0, v1.36.0, v1.36.1, v1.54.1, v1.54.2
findings.evidence: releasing.md:157 says no tag is cut without a bundle whose release field names it; set difference of tags minus manifest release values leaves six tags since 2026-09-08 (v1.54.1/v1.54.2 five minutes apart). Four-suite gate not evaluated for versions vendored into eleven consumers.
findings.remediation: Add a mechanical precondition to docs/releasing.md step 7: `grep -l '"release": "<X.Y.Z>"' docs/automated-tests/*/manifest.json` must print at least one path, and the stamp being tagged from must be one of them (the newest, clean, all-pass bundle). Do not require exactly one: re-runs for the same release are normal (1.35.0 has five). Do not fabricate bundles. Name the six tags once in the next release ANALYSIS.md. At close-out, verify that the new tag appears in at least one manifest.
findings.verify_reason: I checked each tag against the manifest release fields. Since 2026-09-08, exactly v1.28.0, v1.29.0, v1.36.0, v1.36.1, v1.54.1 and v1.54.2 have no bundle naming them, and v1.54.1/v1.54.2 were tagged 5 minutes apart. docs/releasing.md step 7 says 'No tag is cut without a bundle whose release field names it'. The evidence holds. The remediation's precondition is wrong, though. Several releases legitimately have more than one bundle: 1.35.0 has 5, and 1.30.0, 1.31.0, 1.32.0 and 1.36.2 have 2-3 each. An 'exactly one path' check would wrongly block those, and so would the 'exactly one manifest' close-out check.

findings.remediation: Add register row 5 at CLAUDE.md:77: Rule layout-§1; testkit/framework.lua over cap at 1583; Why condensed from :154-165; Decided 2026-09-23; Re-check trigger from :131. Update :78 to 'Five rows'; repoint census cell to 'Register row (layout-§1, 2026-09-23)'. Or, by owner choice, open an issue and repoint :131.
findings.verify_reason: The CLAUDE.md census row for testkit/framework.lua (1583) says 'Ratified deviation row'. The Documented deviations register has four rows (three localization-§5, one compat), and the text after it says 'Four rows'. No row cites layout-§1. The file's own rule says 'a deviation not in the register is not ratified'. layout-§1 (layout.md:67) names three terminal states, one of them 'a ratified deviation row under ## Documented deviations', so the census claims a state that does not exist. The remediation (add register row 5 or open an issue) matches the owner-choice note already in CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: Release runs ship without ANALYSIS.md and docs/releasing.md never asks for one
findings.evidence: v1.55.0 release bundle has no ANALYSIS.md; 32 of 38 release-stamped bundles since 2026-09-08 lack one; grep -ci analysis docs/releasing.md returns 0. 20260916-093057/ANALYSIS.md:60-62 misreads a release run's missing write-up as 'not a breach'. Recurs from 2026-09-08.
findings.remediation: Add numbered sub-step to releasing.md step 7 (write <stamp>/ANALYSIS.md per AUTOMATED_TESTS.md prompt) and test -f <stamp>/ANALYSIS.md to the hard-precondition block; write-up rides in the bundle commit before the tag. No backfill; next ANALYSIS.md notes the gap once and corrects :60-62's reading. After: grep -ci analysis docs/releasing.md >= 1.
findings.verify_reason: The v1.55.0 release bundle 20260923-144526 has only complexity/lint/manifest/test-cases/tests files and no ANALYSIS.md. Of the release-stamped bundles since 1.26.0, only 1.39.0 and 1.50.0-1.54.0 carry one. `grep -ci analysis docs/releasing.md` returns 0. automated-tests-§5 (automated-tests.md:327) says MUST for every release run and forbids backfill. 20260916-093057/ANALYSIS.md:60-62 calls 20260916-033929's missing ANALYSIS.md 'not a breach', but that bundle is the 1.38.0 release run, so the reading is wrong. The remediation (forward-only, plus a precondition in step 7) matches §5.

findings.title: Release notes stopped stating the perf skip
findings.locations: CHANGELOG.md:13-507 (v1.55.0); CHANGELOG.md:583-605 (v1.53.0); CHANGELOG.md:579-581 (v1.54.0 model); docs/releasing.md step 7

findings.title: 210 British spellings in 33 live authored files
findings.locations: tests/ (151 lines, 23 files); live docs/api/ highest-version docs (25 in 5); docs/releasing.md (10); README.md (4); DEPENDENCIES.md (1); tools/artwork/*.py (19 in 2); CLAUDE.md:75 (register row 3)
findings.evidence: Published BRITISH (91) / ALLOWED (30) lists with testkit/test_prose.lua's matcher; excludes ratified payload hits (rows 1, 2) and 560 lines in superseded docs/api records. Register row 3 ratifies gate scope, not the spellings; its trigger names the tests/ sweep as owed. Recurs (216 in 33 on 2026-09-08).
findings.remediation: As proposed (re-run the counter at HEAD, sweep with the published lists, never touch superseded docs/api versions, leave the quoted 'was -> is' lines), with two explicit exclusions. First, leave `.cancelled` / `IsCancelled` member accesses that model AceTimer/C_Timer handles (e.g. tests/test_mock_ace.lua:237,415,443-444,465); either extend register row 1 and tests/test_prose.lua's RATIFIED to cover that path, or keep them as identifiers and fix only the surrounding prose (e.g. test names such as tests/test_perf_core.lua:383 'a cancelled run'). Second, leave tests/test_prose.lua's own quoted forbidden-word fixtures. Target 0 prose hits and update register row 3's figures.
findings.verify_reason: A spot grep of 15 common British forms outside tests/_kit found 98 hits across README.md, docs/releasing.md, 19 tests/ files and tools/artwork/icon_cleaner.py. That is consistent with the claimed ~210 under the full 91-word list, and localization-§5 requires US English. Register row 3 names the tests/ sweep as owed. Two kinds of hit in scope are not prose, and the remediation's check for third-party identifiers only partly covers them. tests/test_mock_ace.lua:237/415/443-444/465 assert AceTimer's real `.cancelled` field, a third-party identifier like register row 1. tests/test_prose.lua quotes forbidden spellings in order to forbid them (9+ hits). Sweeping either mechanically would break the tests.

findings.title: Kit runner emits 'None.' prose instead of a headed table for empty watch-list sets
findings.evidence: '### Functions lizard warned on' followed by 'None.'; both emitters printf 'None.' and return on empty set, while automated-tests-§4 requires a table with header row. Kit vendored byte-identically into eleven consumers, so every consumer's record has the defect. Recurs unchanged.
findings.remediation: Track C (kit revision 25->26): print header + separator unconditionally, no data rows (or one '| — | … |' row) for empty set; drop 'None.' early return; self-test asserting header on empty set; bump Kit.VERSION, docs/api/testkit/version-26-docs.md, regenerate members JSON (lua tools/gen-api-members.lua), CHANGELOG entry; sync testkit/ -> tests/_kit/ same commit. Batch with the review's kit changes (C-02 survey, C-09 asserts.lua) into one kit revision so consumers re-vendor once; re-vendor all eleven.
findings.verify_reason: In testkit/run-automated-tests.sh, fn_table (line 714) and band_table (line 731) each start with `if [ -z ... ]; then printf 'None.\n'; return; fi` before the header printf. docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md prints '### Functions `lizard` warned on' followed by 'None.'. automated-tests.md §4 says the file MUST carry the watch list 'as two tables with header rows'. It does not carve out an empty set, so the finding is a literal but fair reading, and low severity fits. tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh is byte-identical to testkit/ (cmp). Kit.VERSION is 25 (testkit/framework.lua:20), so 25->26 is right. Routing as upstream=false is correct because this repo is where the kit is authored. The fix then reaches consumers through a re-vendor, as the remediation says.

findings.title: Payload registers client events raw on private frames with no pcall'd per-event isolation or rejected-name record
findings.evidence: f:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED"/"PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED") on combat-lock frame and m:RegisterEvent("GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN") on popup menu; events-frames-taint-§1 (binds per library-stack-§7) requires a single pcall'd helper, player-reachable rejected-name record, AceEvent over private frames. Not reachable today; no register row records why. Note: the library cannot floor on consumer-vendored AceEvent (library-stack-§6), a tension the audit resolves locally via a register row rather than flagging against the standard.
findings.remediation: Record a CLAUDE.md register row for events-frames-taint-§1. It covers the widget-owned private frames in OptionsTabs.lua (combat lock, PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/ENABLED) and Widgets.lua (popup-menu dismiss, GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN). Reasons: the section is written against addon event traffic; these frames carry UI state for one widget; and the three names are stable core events, so one-bad-name isolation cannot trigger. Do not justify the row with 'the library cannot use AceEvent', because Bus.lua already resolves AceEvent at call time. Re-check trigger: registering any event newer than the current expansion, or a fourth private registration site. Make no code change unless the owner chooses the pcall'd-helper route. If they do, batch it with the OptionsTabs/Widgets minors already planned.
findings.verify_reason: The cited call sites are real: OptionsTabs.lua:102-103 and :139-140 (PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/ENABLED on lib.__combatFrame) and Widgets.lua:393 (GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN on the popup menu). No CLAUDE.md register row mentions events-frames-taint. Two parts of the evidence are wrong, though. (1) library-stack-§7's 'every rule above applies' refers to library-stack's own earlier rules (§1-§6). It does not import events-frames-taint-§1, and §1's text is addressed to an addon (`addon:RegisterEvent`, a module's disable path, the player-facing debug verb). The binding is therefore interpretive, not the stated rule. (2) The claim that the library 'cannot floor on consumer-vendored AceEvent' is contradicted by the library itself: library-stack-§7's Bus row says Bus.lua resolves AceEvent-3.0 at call time. The reachable impact is nil. All three names are stable core client events, and the per-event-isolation clause exists to stop one retired name from deafening a block, which cannot happen with PLAYER_REGEN_*/GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN. These are widget-owned UI frames, not addon event traffic. Info fits better than low. Option (b), a register row, is the right disposition. Option (a) adds a helper, minors and a re-vendor for no reachable benefit.
